chief_complaint: jaw pain, malocclusion, and bleeding gums after trauma
hpi_details: A 44-year-old woman presents after facial trauma with jaw pain, malocclusion, and bleeding gums. She reports worsening pain with chewing and is concerned that her teeth no longer meet normally.
ideas: thinks it might be related to jaw_fracture
concerns: worried about potential complications and long term recovery
expectations: wants complete diagnostic evaluation and treatment plan

investigation_events.title: Emergency maxillofacial CT
investigation_events.availability_message: The emergency maxillofacial CT result is now available. Continue airway assessment and urgent oral-maxillofacial surgical involvement.

results.value: Displaced fracture through the left mandibular body with a 4 mm step-off and disruption of dental occlusion; no condylar dislocation

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Mandible Fracture is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes maxillofacial CT and urgent specialist assessment; closed treatment or open reduction and internal fixation is selected according to fracture pattern, displacement, occlusion, and patient factors.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: jaw pain, malocclusion, and bleeding gums after trauma
Key HPI features: Facial trauma followed by jaw pain, malocclusion, gingival bleeding, and pain with chewing.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Mandible Fracture.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Mandible Fracture.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue infection without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Missing airway compromise, uncontrolled bleeding, or associated head and cervical-spine injury after facial trauma.
management_principles: Plan for Mandible Fracture: Maxillofacial CT, open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF)
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of jaw pain, malocclusion, and bleeding gums after trauma. HPI: facial bone fracture.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Mandible Fracture.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Mandible Fracture.
reference_soap.plan: Obtain maxillofacial CT and urgently involve oral and maxillofacial surgery. Manage with closed treatment or ORIF according to fracture pattern, displacement, and occlusion; assess the airway and provide analgesia and oral-care instructions.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Mandible Fracture
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Mandible Fracture
Implement evidence-based management plan: Maxillofacial CT, open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF)

teaching.one_liner: Plastic and reconstructive surgical case presenting with jaw pain, malocclusion, and bleeding gums after trauma.
red_flags: Difficulty breathing, swallowing secretions, drooling, voice change, or uncontrolled oral bleeding requiring immediate airway assessment
Altered consciousness, vomiting, focal neurologic symptoms, or other high-energy trauma requiring emergency evaluation

must_ask.say: How did you injure your jaw, and when did it happen?
Do your teeth fit together the way they used to, and is your lip or chin numb?
Are your gums bleeding, and are you having any trouble breathing or swallowing?

must_ask.objective: Loss of consciousness or associated injuries
must_ask.say: Did you lose consciousness or injure any other part of your body?

must_ask.objective: Alcohol use and prior facial trauma
must_ask.say: Had you been drinking before the injury, and have you had facial trauma before?
